decisions.text: type bar: the periods are the point
Expenses as bars, Budget as a flat marker across each bar: the bars feature the individual categories or periods, the reference stays in the background (G1.60, D-21)
Budget, a reference, as a flat marker across each bar of Expenses, in the strong shade of the bar's hue, on the bars' zero-based scale (G1.60, G7.57)
time runs left to right: vertical bars
digits hidden: thousands, stated once on the top label (R2-05, D-3): “$120K (expenses per month)”
time axis: row 2 (“2022”) left out, the title gives it (G2.37)
the unit phrase on the top label: “$120K (expenses per month)”; the top gridline starts after it
Expenses and Budget named once, beside the last bar, the first having no room, with thin grey leaders (G5.5, D-7)

source.shows: the book's good combo for individual months against a reference: light bars and a flat budget marker across each; beside the first bar the names would meet March's bar, so they stand beside the last, as the book puts them (G5.5, D-7). The book's first version, bars with the budget as a line, cannot be asked for: a series' mark type follows its role, never a choice made for variety (G1.59)
